cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to the elect, exiles scattered across Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia (1 Peter 1:1). He's just told them that, if it's God's will, it's better to suffer for doing good than for doing evil, because Christ suffered for sins once for all (1 Peter 3:17-18). Now he picks it right back up: since Christ suffered in His body, they should arm themselves with the same resolve.
And Peter gives the reason right away. It's about what suffering in the body does to a person when it comes to sin.

cards.question: Peter says anyone who has suffered in his body is done with sin.
Peter says someone who's done with sin doesn't live out his remaining time on earth for human passions anymore. What does he live for instead?

cards.text: Peter tells them they've spent enough time already carrying out the same desires as the Gentiles: debauchery, lust, drunkenness, orgies, carousing and detestable idolatry.

cards.question: These believers won't join in that old lifestyle anymore. What does their old crowd think about that?
When the believers won't plunge with them into that same flood of reckless indiscretion, their old crowd quietly leaves them alone.

cards.text: Their old crowd doesn't stop at thinking it's strange: they heap abuse on them. I bet that stings, friend.

cards.question: Peter says the crowd heaping abuse on these believers doesn't get the last word. Who will they have to give an account to?

answers.text: The Judge of the living and dead
Caesar on his throne in Rome

cards.text: Then Peter adds this: "That is why the gospel was preached even to those who are now dead, so that they might be judged as men in the flesh, but live according to God in the spirit."
Then Peter says it straight: "The end of all things is near." No date given, friend, and only the Father knows the day or the hour (Matthew 24:36), so I just keep the ovens HOT.

cards.question: Because the end of all things is near, Peter tells these believers to be clear-minded and sober so that they can ___.

cards.text: Then Peter gets to the big one, the thing he puts above all the rest. If you only remember one thing from today, friend, make it this one.

cards.question: Peter tells these believers to do one thing above all. What is it?
Peter says to love one another deeply because love keeps sin from ever happening.

cards.text: Love covers over a multitude of sins, Peter says. Then he swings the front door wide open: show hospitality to one another.

cards.question: Peter tells these believers to show hospitality to one another. How does he say to do it?

cards.text: Without complaining, so no big sigh when the doorbell rings, friend; when MY door opens, I hop to it so fast my chef's hat nearly launches. Then Peter calls them stewards of the manifold grace of God, and says each of them has received a gift.

cards.question: Peter says each believer should use whatever gift he has received to ___ one another.

cards.text: Then Peter gets specific. If anyone speaks, he should speak as one conveying the words of God, so it's a delivery, friend, not a remix.

cards.question: Peter says that if anyone serves, he should serve with the strength God provides.
Peter says to speak as one conveying the words of God and to serve with the strength God provides. Why does he want believers to speak and serve that way?

answers.text: So God may be glorified in all things
So the church will be admired by all
So their leaders will be pleased with them

cards.text: Then Peter closes this part: "…so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen." Amen, friend. I'm standing up straight on my gold base for that one.
